title: Evaluating Token Probabilities as Confidence Estimators in Human Behavior Simulations: A Case Study in Luxembourgish Next Like Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2611.07735v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior, their operational validity is typically assessed through accuracy alone, implicitly treating human behavior as deterministic. We argue that on noisy digital trace data, a model's performance depends not only on predicting the correct outcome but on its calibration. We present a case study testing whether the token probabilities of open-weight LLMs can serve as confidence estimates in a Next Like Prediction task: predicting how a user of the Luxembourgish news platform RTL.lu rates a comment, conditioned on their prior interactions. Evaluating Ministral 3 (3B, 8B), we find that, with in-context learning only, the tested models are overconfident and are outperformed on accuracy and calibration by a simple statistical baseline. translated_title: 评估Token概率作为人类行为模拟中的置信度估计器：以卢森堡语下一次点赞预测为例的案例研究
translated_abstract: 随着大型语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于模拟人类行为，其操作有效性通常仅通过准确率来评估，这隐含地将人类行为视为确定性的。我们认为，在嘈杂的数字痕迹数据上，模型的性能不仅取决于预测出正确的结果，还取决于其校准程度。我们开展了一项案例研究，测试开放权重LLM的token概率能否在“下一次点赞预测”任务中作为置信度估计：即在用户先前交互行为的条件下，预测卢森堡新闻平台RTL.lu的用户会如何对评论进行评分。通过评估Ministral 3（3B、8B），我们发现仅使用上下文学习时，被测模型表现出过度自信，且在准确率和校准度上均被简单的统计基线所超越。准确率与校准度并不同步变化：从3B扩展到8B提升了准确率却降低了校准度，而更长的行为……（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 本研究以卢森堡新闻平台的点赞预测任务为例，发现LLM的token概率作为置信度估计时模型过度自信、被简单统计基线全面超越，且准确率与校准度并不同步——扩大模型规模能提升准确率却损害校准度，表明评估人类行为模拟时校准度是不可忽视的关键指标。
en_tdlr: In a Luxembourgish next-like prediction case study, LLM token probabilities serve as overconfident confidence estimates that are outperformed by a simple statistical baseline, and scaling from 3B to 8B improves accuracy while degrading calibration, showing that calibration must be evaluated alongside accuracy in human behavior simulations.
